threat_register.name: Agent goal manipulation
threat_register.surface: The RAG corpus is text the crew reads before writing a memo. A document carrying an instruction rather than a fact could redirect what the memo concludes.
threat_register.control: Retrieved text is fenced in <retrieved> delimiters and quoted as data. The Auditor blocks a memo containing advice language whatever produced it, so a successful injection still cannot ship.

threat_register.name: Tool misuse
threat_register.surface: Six agents share one tool registry. The Advisor writes the recommendation, so it is the agent an attacker most wants holding a tool.
threat_register.control: The Advisor is granted the empty set. The registry refuses any call from an agent without an explicit grant, and the Auditor blocks the run if the Advisor called anything at all or was granted anything at all.

threat_register.name: Identity and privilege abuse
threat_register.surface: The API separates viewer, analyst and admin. Memo writing is the only endpoint that writes, so it is the privilege worth stealing.
threat_register.control: The role arrives in a header the deployment's gateway sets, and anything unrecognised degrades to viewer rather than escalating. Endpoints declare a minimum role and return 403 below it.

threat_register.name: Resource overload
threat_register.surface: A crew run makes model requests in a loop. An input that makes the loop longer costs quota, and quota is the one budget this project cannot buy more of.
threat_register.control: Two controls, because they fail differently. Three budgets — requests, seconds and steps — bound a single run. Rate limits bound how many runs a caller can start: a stranger who begins two hundred well-behaved runs spends the day's quota just as completely as one runaway loop.

threat_register.name: Resource overload by volume
threat_register.surface: Before authentication existed, `/memos` was an unauthenticated stranger's button for running an agent crew, and `/ask` still needs no account by design.
threat_register.control: A token bucket per caller: generous on reads, tight on `/ask`, tighter on `/memos`, which additionally requires an analyst credential. Buckets are per process, which is exact on one instance and would need a shared counter on two.

threat_register.name: Cascading reliability failure
threat_register.surface: The provider chain falls Ollama to Gemini to Groq. A hop that fails loudly could take the whole request down with it.
threat_register.control: Each hop is caught and logged, and the chain ends at a deterministic offline provider, so a feature degrades to a plainer answer instead of a 500.

threat_register.name: Memory and context poisoning
threat_register.surface: Memory is text one run writes and a later run reads. A note phrased as an instruction would steer every run after it.
threat_register.control: Notes are screened on the way in and quarantined — not deleted — when they read as instructions. Quarantined entries never reach a prompt and are listed in the audit.

threat_register.name: Insecure inter-agent communication
threat_register.surface: Agents coordinate over a shared bus; the memo is defended by its transcript.
threat_register.control: Every message is HMAC-signed and the log is append-only and ordered. The Auditor verifies all signatures and blocks the run if any message fails.

threat_register.name: Untraceable decision-making
threat_register.surface: A number with no provenance is the failure this whole project is built against: a plausible figure nobody can check is worse than no figure.
threat_register.control: Every KPI carries the SQL that produced it and cannot be constructed without it. Every factual memo sentence carries a citation or is removed before the memo ships.

threat_register.name: Agentic supply chain
threat_register.surface: Python and npm dependencies, and the model weights the provider chain reaches.
threat_register.control: Locked dependency files, `pip-audit` and `npm audit` in CI, and no model weights downloaded at runtime — the offline embedder is fitted from the corpus itself.

threat_register.name: Human manipulation
threat_register.surface: The product's output is a memo about money. Confident prose is itself the attack surface: a reader who believes a hedged statistical estimate is a recommendation has been manipulated whether or not anyone intended it.
threat_register.control: No transaction endpoint exists anywhere in the API. Advice language is blocked in the memo, an 'information, not advice' notice sits on every page carrying a conclusion, and disagreement between the Valuer and the RiskAuditor is shown rather than resolved.

threat_register.name: Unauthorised transaction execution
threat_register.surface: Absent: no endpoint, tool or agent can place, fund or settle anything.
threat_register.control: `tests/test_api.py` asserts no route path segment matches a transaction verb.

threat_register.name: Data exfiltration by an agent
threat_register.surface: Absent: no agent holds a network tool, so there is nowhere to send data.
threat_register.control: The registry's whole tool set is read-only queries against the local warehouse.
